summary: Reproduced the list-element truncation bypass in both JSON and text request-log formatting, then made list and tuple formatting recursively truncate every retained element, including elements retained by head/tail elision. Added regressions for both reported paths and independent exact-boundary and tuple-format cases.

tests.what_was_measured: Four CPU unit tests covering JSON elided-list element truncation, text-list element truncation, the exact list-length boundary, and elided tuple formatting; 4 passed.

The original million-character fixture was executed inline: JSON output for 2,049 elements fell from the extrapolated/raw-branch ~2 GB behavior to 4,208,647 bytes, every retained element was 2,051 characters, and text output for ten elements was 20,590 bytes with no full input element present. The exact inline output is retained in raw/reproduction-after.txt.
No whitespace errors in the implementation, tests, or report changes.

gpu_execution.evidence: The affected helpers are pure Python serialization functions and the source issue's reproduction is explicitly CPU-only; GPU execution would not exercise a different implementation path.

remaining_limitations: No HTTP server or model was run because the defect and correction are confined to pure Python formatting helpers.
No GPU test was run because GPU hardware is not relevant to these helpers.
Ruff was unavailable in both the prepared interpreter and PATH; focused pytest and git diff --check completed successfully.
